title: Japanese Imperial Era Calendar
intro: Japan often labels years by the reigning emperor's official era, while retaining Gregorian month and day numbering in modern civil life.
summary: A modern Gregorian date with an imperial-era label and a year counted from that era's beginning.
origin: Japan's modern era system includes Meiji, Taisho, Showa, Heisei and Reiwa. The Gregorian calendar was adopted for civil use in 1873.
structure: An imperial era changes when the era officially begins; the era year resets to 1 even if the Gregorian year is already underway.
diagram_caption: ERA NAME + YEAR NUMBER + ORDINARY DATE
pattern_note: The year a new era begins is known as its first year (gannen). An era year need not start on 1 January.
history: Era names remain common in official forms and everyday references in Japan. Changes can occur within a Gregorian calendar year when imperial succession takes place.
example: The Gregorian year 2026 is Reiwa 8. A date in April 2019 was Heisei 31, but a date in May 2019 is Reiwa 1.
limits: Before 1 January 1873 Japanese civil calendar dates were lunisolar. Projecting modern Gregorian months backward into Meiji years 1–5 is not historic Japanese civil notation.
